newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Bank of Greece has recommended to the government that it forge ahead with changes as soon as possible to the job market and to the social insurance system, with governor Lucas Papademos saying that the pension fund finances and the demographic problem would bring the social security system to crisis.

--Leading government members yesterday expressed their fears that a recent letter of protest by 32 ruling party MPs to the government's plans for Greek-Turkish dialogue was only the tip of the iceberg in internal dissent. There is more dissent on the horizon, they said, particularly in regard to the government's positions on changes to the job market and to local and regional government.
--An inquiry is under way into claims that 200 tonnes of toxic waste has been moved to a local garbage dump to save the costs of disposing it safely.

--The discussion on a Greek-Turkish rapprochement is being bolstered with talks at the US State Department between Madeleine Albright and European Commissioner Hans van den Broek considering recent developments "very important".
--Greek basketball team Olympiakos won its match in Rome last night and will face Barcelona tomorrow night.

--The economic crimes squad SDOE will receive more powers which will enable them to supervise and check every financial activity in the wider public sector, including the fate of subsidies from European Community programmes.
--Retirement ages will be set at age 65 for men and 65 for women and workers in hazardous professions, reports say, as of January 1998.
--A confidential report from the Italian counter-espionage service has accused Greece of underhanded dealings in provoking the recent crisis in Albania.
